video_title: RJ Explains Why Jalen Brunson Has the MOST to Gain in the NBA Finals

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson has the most to gain in the NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: When I look at who has the most to gain from how many opportunities will he get

text_blocks.speaker: Allie Clifton
text_blocks.text: Currently right now, let's look at Willis Reed, two chips, two Finals MVP, seven... No, we're not talking about him. You said about Brunson. I said with the players that will be playing in the Finals, SGA, Wembanyama, or Brunson. Who has the most to gain?

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: 1,000%. I think if we were to kind of lay it out, the Knicks are having a magical season. The way their players are shooting, everything coming together, kind of the tweak of the offense, historic run. But I look at it as, Wembanyama, we feel like Wembanyama might have eight more chances at this. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, he's already won a championship and has two MVPs in his back pocket. Brunson is a guy that hasn't won an MVP, hasn't won a Finals MVP, hasn't won a championship. So when I look at who has the most to gain from how many opportunities will he get, this Knicks team, maybe they win two championships over the next five years. But we're not looking at them as the consistent favorite out of their conference, and they wouldn't be the favorite here. So when you get that moment and you get that opportunity, it needs to be seized.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's greatness will be determined over the next five to seven years
quotes.excerpt: His greatness in my opinion is going to be determined over the next five to seven years
quotes.quote: Wembanyama, I wish he had a 15 or 20-year career. But history tells us that guys that are 7'4" and higher don't really have that long of a window. So over the next five or six years, Wembanyama has to max out. His greatness in my opinion is going to be determined over the next five to seven years. I just don't know at 7'5" and I hope I'm wrong, but like you say, with the facts, my opinion could change. But these are facts. If you look at the history of greats, like Yao Ming and all those guys over 7', they didn't have that long window. But Shaquille O'Neal made a great point. I saw him on a podcast. He said this reminds him, whether it's OKC or the Spurs, it's going to remind him of when Detroit beat the Lakers in 2004. They were playing some great basketball, walked into the Finals as a serious-ass underdog.

quotes.speaker: Allie Clifton
quotes.summary_phrase: Players who won regular season MVP and championship in back-to-back seasons
quotes.excerpt: Only three players in NBA history have achieved this rare feat

text_blocks.speaker: Allie Clifton
text_blocks.text: Only three players in NBA history have achieved this rare feat of winning both the regular season MVP and an NBA championship in back-to-back seasons. Who are they?

text_blocks.speaker: Allie Clifton
text_blocks.text: You are correct, Bill Russell, Jordan. It's after Jordan. It's after Jordan.

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: Kobe didn't win, Shaq only got what MVP, regular season MVP, Kobe only got one regular season MVP. Who has... I forgot that bitch beat us in OKC. That motherfucker.
